rationale: No analog interface; pure digital serial protocol

extraction_strategy.ic_class_applicability_gate_v0_1_62: ic_class='serial_peripheral_protocol' declares LL5 not applicable; emitted as N/A stub (l_doc_taxonomy.na_stub)

signaling_summary: FC-0 physical layer: a serial, full-duplex link of one transmit and one receive lane (differential copper or optical fibre). NRZ signaling at 1/2/4/8/16/32 GFC and PAM-4 at 64GFC; 128GFC aggregates four 32GFC lanes. The clock is embedded (recovered at the receiver with CDR). FC-1 line encoding is 8b/10b (1/2/4/8 GFC) or 64b/66b (16 GFC and above) with running disparity and word synchronization. Signaling rate is negotiated to the highest mutually supported rate, with backward compatibility to lower rates.
modulation: NRZ at 1/2/4/8/16/32 GFC; PAM-4 at 64GFC; differential/optical, embedded-clock.
clocking: Embedded clock recovered by the receiver (clock-data recovery); spread-spectrum clocking optional. NOT a forwarded/source-synchronous clock.

transmitter_specs_canonical.interop_rule: Negotiate the highest common rate; support backward compatibility to lower rates.

receiver_specs_canonical.word_synchronization: Aligns on the K28.5-based comma character / ordered-set boundary.
receiver_specs_canonical.running_disparity: Tracked for 8b/10b; 64b/66b uses scrambling + sync header.

encoding_role_in_analog: 8b/10b (<=8 GFC) provides DC balance and transition density for clock recovery and word alignment; 64b/66b (>=16 GFC) uses a 2-bit sync header plus scrambling for lower overhead at high rate. Frame integrity is provided digitally by the 32-bit CRC over the FC-2 frame header + payload.
